result.topic_en: Euler splits the solution y into two parts y = αp + gq and determines the power-series coefficients of p and q from two derived integro-differential equations, in his study of the height at which columns buckle under their own weight.
result.transcription:
) 180 (

§. 27. Hinc ergo ſtatim valorem ipſius $y$ in duas partes diuellere poterimus, quae ſint $y = \alpha p + g q$; hoc autem valore introducto aequatio noſtra erit
$g x + \alpha \int x\, dp + g \int x\, dq + m\alpha . \frac{ddp}{dx^2} . m g . \frac{ddq}{dx^2} = 0$.
vnde hae duae aequationes deriuantur:
I. $\int x\, dp + m \frac{ddp}{dx^2} = 0$.
II. $x + \int x\, dq + m \frac{ddq}{dx^2} = 0$.
Pro priore, quoniam nouimus, primum terminum ipſius $p$ eſſe $x$, ſtatuamus $p = x - A x^4 + B x^7 + C x^{10} + \text{etc.}$ factaque ſubſtitutione perueniemus ad ſequentem aequationem:
$0 = \begin{cases} \frac{m\,ddp}{dx^2} = -4.3 m A x^2 + 7.6 m B x^5 - 10.9 m C x^8 + 13.12. m D x^{11} \text{ etc.} \\ \int x\, dp = \frac{1}{2} x x - \frac{4}{5} A x^5 + \frac{7}{8} B x^8 - \frac{10}{11} C x^{11} + \text{etc.} \end{cases}$
vnde ergo coefficientes aſſumti ſequenti modo determinantur:
$A = \frac{1}{2.3.4.m}$; $B = \frac{4A}{5.6.7.m} = \frac{1.4.}{2.3.\ldots.7 m^2}$,
$C = \frac{7B}{8.9.10.m} = \frac{1.4.7.}{2.3.\ldots.10. m^3}$
$D = \frac{10 C}{11.12.13.m} = \frac{1.4.7.10.}{2.3.\ldots.13. m^4}$, etc.
Pro valore ipſius $q$, ex altera aequatione eruendo, fingamus $q = -\mathfrak{A} x^3 + \mathfrak{B} x^6 - \mathfrak{C} x^9 + \mathfrak{D} x^{12} - \text{etc.}$ et facta ſubſtitutione perueniemus ad hanc aequationem:
$\left. \begin{matrix} \frac{m\,ddq}{dx^2} = -3.2 m \mathfrak{A} x + 6.5 m \mathfrak{B} x^4 - 9.8 m \mathfrak{C} x^7 + 12.11 m \mathfrak{D} x^{10} - \text{etc.} \\ \int x\, dq = \quad - \frac{3}{4} \mathfrak{A} x^4 + \frac{6}{7} \mathfrak{B} x^7 - \frac{9}{10} \mathfrak{C} x^{10} + \text{etc.} \\ + x = + 1. x \quad - \; - \; - \; - \; - \; - \; - \end{matrix} \right\} = 0$
vnde ergo coefficientes aſſumti ſequenti modo determinabuntur:
